title: A neighbourhood in the heat
question: Where can a resident find relief on a hot afternoon?
summary: Follow a resident from home to school, across sun-exposed paving, through a shaded park and into a community cool room. Surfaces, shade and an open door shape the journey.

presentation.intro: The same hot day. Different surfaces, shade and access to relief.
presentation.storyHeading: Relief is more than a nearby building.
presentation.caption: Follow the people, the conditions and the door that must be open.

entities.label: Resident's home
entities.description: The resident leaves home to collect a child from school, following the school's heat-day notice.
entities.constraint: The pickup route needs to suit the family's mobility and walking distance.

entities.label: Linden school
entities.description: A classroom opens onto the neighbourhood. Staff share a heat-day notice with families, and the resident meets the child at the nearby square.
entities.constraint: Families rely on the school to pass on current opening information for the community room.

entities.label: Sunlit square
entities.role: Exposed meeting point and paved surface
entities.description: The family meets on a paved square beside the school. Sun-exposed paving absorbs and re-emits heat.
entities.constraint: The waiting area has little shade, so the family moves to the park path after pickup.

entities.label: Canopy park
entities.description: Mature trees shade parts of the path and seating area. Vegetation also cools through evapotranspiration. The family takes this route toward the community room.
entities.constraint: Shade shifts with the sun. The route follows the shaded parts of the maintained path.

entities.label: Community cool room
entities.description: An indoor meeting room offers seats, drinking water and mechanical cooling. In the first story it is open; in the second, the resident arrives after an unexpected closure.
entities.constraint: The room needs an open entrance, staff, power and working cooling to receive visitors.

relationships.label: Resident walks to school for pickup
Family meets at the exposed square
Family moves from the square to the shaded park path
Family walks from the park to the community room
Family returns to park shade after finding the room closed
Community staff publish opening information to the school
School shares the heat-day notice with families
Sun-exposed paving can contribute to outdoor heat exposure beside the school
The school community's indoor respite depends on the room being open and functioning

scenarios.label: A hot afternoon
scenarios.summary: From pickup to shade and an indoor break.
scenarios.condition: The resident can make this walk. The park path is accessible, and the community cool room is open with working cooling.
scenarios.outcome: The family reaches the community room for an indoor break after using the shaded park path.

steps.title: Walk to school
steps.text: The resident in the ochre coat leaves home to collect the child, following the school's heat-day notice.

steps.title: Wait on exposed paving
steps.text: The family meets at the largely unshaded square. The paving absorbs and re-emits solar heat, and the family waits in direct sun.

steps.title: Move into patchy shade
steps.text: They take the park path to get out of direct sun. The tree canopy provides shade, and vegetation cools through evapotranspiration.

steps.title: Reach an open cool room
steps.text: The family enters the community room for an indoor break. Seats, drinking water and working cooling are available inside.

scenarios.label: A closed door
scenarios.summary: An outdated notice leads to a closed entrance.
scenarios.condition: The family is at the park and relies on an outdated opening notice. The community room has closed unexpectedly.
scenarios.outcome: They return to park shade without reaching indoor refuge. They still need another indoor place to take a break.

steps.title: Follow the old notice
steps.text: The family leaves the park for the room using previously published information. The entrance is already closed, although the resident has not discovered this yet.

steps.title: The room is closed
steps.text: The family reaches a closed entrance. The room's unexpected closure has not reached them through the school's notice.

steps.title: Return to shade
steps.text: The family returns to the park. They wait in the shade while looking for another indoor place to take a break.

state.caption: Back in shade; indoor refuge unresolved
